Rashi on Eruvin 30b:10:1.hebrew: דלית ליה שיעורא - שמזון ב' סעודות מצומצמות הניח, ואי מפריש תרומה מיניה כל דהו — בצר ליה שיעור עירוב:
Rashi on Eruvin 30b:10:1.english: Where it does not have the [requisite] measure - For he deposited food [for] precisely two meals, and if he separates any teruma at all from it, the [requisite] measure of the eiruv will be lacking.

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:11:1.hebrew: ומאי פסקא - בתמיה. כלומר: מאי האי תירוצא? וכי פסקא תנא למילתיה דאין אדם נותן עירובו אלא בצמצום, דנקט סתם במילתיה הכי:
Rashi on Eruvin 30b:11:1.english: And what makes it definite - [This is asked] in astonishment. That is to say: What kind of resolution is this? Did the Tanna establish his ruling [so definitively, assuming] that a person deposits his eiruv only with an exact measure, that he formulated his statement unconditionally like this?

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:11:2.english: Holds in accordance with the Rabbis - Who disagree with Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] below (Eruvin 34b).

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:11:3.hebrew: גזרו עליו בין השמשות - כבשבת עצמה, והגבהת תרומה שבות היא. וכיון דמעיקרא לא תקנה, ובעית למימר: אי בעי הוי חזי לההוא שעתא — דמתשיל עלה כל מקום שהיא, והדרה לטבלא, והדר אמר: תרומתה בצפון שבה ומעשר ראשון בדרומה, וכן כולם — אם כן, מתקן ליה בין השמשות וקעבר אשבות, וקניית עירוב כשזה נכנס וזה יוצא:
Rashi on Eruvin 30b:11:3.english: They decreed against it during twilight - Just as on Shabbat itself; and separating teruma is a rabbinic prohibition [shevut]. And since initially he had not prepared it [to be permissible for him], and [even if] you were to say: If he wished, it would be fit [for him] at that time — since he could request [absolution] for it wherever it is, and it would revert to tevel, and he could then say, "Its teruma is in its northern part, and first tithe is in its southern part," and similarly all of them — if so, he is rectifying it during twilight and violating a shevut; and the acquisition of an eiruv [takes effect] when this [day] enters and that [day] departs.

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:12:1.hebrew: יש שאמרו - יש דברים שאמרו שיעורן לפי מה שהוא אדם, ואין שיעורן שוה בכל:
Rashi on Eruvin 30b:12:1.english: There are [matters] regarding which they said - There are matters regarding which they said their measure is according to what a person is, and their measure is not uniform for everyone.

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:12:2.english: His handfuls of incense - [This is] on Yom Kippur.

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:14:1.hebrew: תרגומא - להא דתלי שיעורא באדם עצמו: אחולה וזקן, ולקולא; ולא ארעבתן, ולחומרא — דבטלה דעתו:
Rashi on Eruvin 30b:14:1.english: Interpret it - [Apply] that which [the Mishnah] made the measure dependent on the person himself to an ill or elderly person, and leniently; and not to a glutton, and stringently — for his standard is disregarded.

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:15:1.hebrew: מנפח אדם בית הפרס - שדה שנחרש בה קבר, דכולה ספיקא משום עצמות היא, ועצמות בלא בשר אינו מטמא באהל. וכשמנפח לפני רגליו, אם יש שם עצם גדול — נראה מאליו, ועצם קטן — נראה בנפיחה, ואינו מסיטו ברגליו:
Rashi on Eruvin 30b:15:1.english: A person may blow [in] a beit haperas - [This refers to] a field in which a grave was plowed, for the entire doubt is on account of [scattered] bones, and bones without flesh do not transmit ritual impurity in a tent. And when he blows before his feet, if there is a large bone there, it is visible on its own, and a small bone is revealed through blowing, and [thus] he will not shift it with his feet.

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:15:2.english: That has been trodden - By the treading of people's feet.

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:15:3.english: Is pure - For the bones in it have already been trodden upon and reduced to less than [the size of] a barley grain.

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:16:1.english: A moving tent - A tent that is moved.

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:16:2.english: Is called a tent - And it interposes between him and the impurity.

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:17:1.english: The land of the nations - Imparts ritual impurity through a tent.

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:17:2.hebrew: שידה - מרכבת נשים, עגלה עשויה כקופסא:
Rashi on Eruvin 30b:17:2.english: A carriage - A women's carriage, a wagon made like a box.

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:17:3.english: A cupboard - Mestier [in Old French, a cupboard for storing food].

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:18:1.english: A moving tent is not called a tent - And whatever is not a tent does not interpose [against impurity].

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:18:2.hebrew: שמיה אוהל - וחוצץ. ובגדולה עסקינן, שמחזקת מ' סאה בלח, שהם כוריים ביבש, דאי קטנה — כלי היא, ומקבלת טומאה, ולא חייצא. ורבנן דמתני' כרבי סבירא להו. ובין לרבי יהודה ובין לרבנן, כסומכוס סבירא להו, דאמר: מידי דחזי ליה למיכליה בההיא שעתא בעינן:
Rashi on Eruvin 30b:18:2.english: It is called a tent - And [therefore] shields [against ritual impurity]. And we are dealing with a large [container], which holds forty se’ah of liquid, which are two kor of dry [measure]; for if [it were] small, it is a vessel, and it is susceptible to ritual impurity, and does not shield. And the Rabbis of our Mishnah hold in accordance with Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi]. And both according to Rabbi Yehuda and according to the Rabbis, they hold in accordance with Sumchus, who said: We require something that is fit for him to eat at that time.

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:1:1.hebrew: שמערבין לגדול - למי שהוא גדול, שהביא שתי שערות, שחייב בענוי. ואע"ג דלמחר לא חזי ליה — הואיל וחזי לקטן, שאינו בר עונשין:
Rashi on Eruvin 30b:1:1.english: That one may establish an eiruv for an adult - For one who is an adult, who has grown two hairs, [and] who is obligated in affliction [of fasting]. And even though on the morrow it is not fit for him [to eat], [it is valid] since it is fit for a minor, who is not subject to punishment.

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:3:1.english: While it was still day - Of the eve of Yom Kippur.

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:4:1.hebrew: כמאן דלא כחנניה - הא מתני', דמשמע שהיו בית שמאי מודין בעירוב — דלא כחנניה:
Rashi on Eruvin 30b:4:1.english: In accordance with whose [opinion]? Not in accordance with Ḥananya - This baraita, which implies that Beit Shammai conceded regarding an eiruv, is not in accordance with Ḥananya.

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:4:2.hebrew: כל כלי תשמישו - משמע דאי לא אפיק כל צרכי תשמיש, לא הוי עירוב לדידיה:
Rashi on Eruvin 30b:4:2.english: All his utensils - This implies that if he did not take out all necessities of use, it is not an eiruv according to him.

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:5:1.hebrew: עירב בשחורים - היה לבוש שחורים, והלך וישב בסוף אלפים אמה עד שקנה שם שביתה שקידש עליו היום, וחזר לביתו:
Rashi on Eruvin 30b:5:1.english: [If] one established an eiruv in black [garments] - He was dressed in black [garments], and went and sat at the end of two thousand cubits until he acquired [Shabbat] residence there when the day became sanctified upon him, and he returned to his home.

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:7:1.hebrew: דמיתשיל אנזירותיה - ישאל לחכם, ויתיר לו נדרו, ויהא יין ראוי לו:
Rashi on Eruvin 30b:7:1.english: That he can ask [to be released] from his nazirite status - He can ask a Sage, who will release his vow for him, and the wine will be suitable for him.

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:8:1.hebrew: מיתשיל עליה - ויפתח בחרטה: ״לא נתכוונתי לכך״, ותנן (נזיר דף לא.): ״הקדש טעות אינו הקדש״:
Rashi on Eruvin 30b:8:1.english: One can ask [a Sage to annul] it - And he opens with regret: “I did not intend this.” And we learned (Nazir 31a): “Mistaken consecration is not consecration.”

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:8:2.english: It returns to tevel - And tevel is not fit [for consumption].

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:9:1.hebrew: וליפרוש עליה ממקום אחר - לבתר דמתשיל עלה והדרא לטבלא, בין השמשות, בשעת קניית עירוב, מצי למימר: ״פירות שיש לי בביתי יהו תרומה על זו״, ואשתכח דאית ליה תקנתא דתחזי ליה:
Rashi on Eruvin 30b:9:1.english: And let him separate [teruma] for it from another place - After he asks [a Sage to annul the designation] for it and it reverts to tevel, at twilight, at the time of the acquisition of the eiruv, he can say: “Produce that I have in my house shall be teruma for this,” and it turns out that he has a remedy so that it is fit for him.

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:9:2.hebrew: מוקף - סמוך, כמו מקיפין בבועי (חולין מו:) — שסומכים זו לזו ורואין אם דומות זו לזו — וכמו מקפת וקורא לה שם דמסכת נדה בפרק בתרא (דף עא:):
Rashi on Eruvin 30b:9:2.english: Mukkaf [nearby] - Adjacent; as in "we bring vesicles close together" (Chullin 46b) — where they place [them] next to one another and see if they resemble each other; and as in "she brings [them] close and designates it by name" in tractate Niddah, in the last chapter (daf 71b).

Rashi on Eruvin 30b:9:3.hebrew: שלא מן המוקף - מדבר שאינו סמוך לו באותו כלי, דליהוי מיניה וביה:
Rashi on Eruvin 30b:9:3.english: Not from that which is adjacent - From something that is not adjacent to it in the same vessel, so that it would be from within itself.

Tosafot on Eruvin 30b:11:1.hebrew: אלא סומכוס סבר לה כרבנן - ואם תאמר: מהאי טעמא נמי, נזיר לא יערב ביין, כיון דשבות הוא לשאול על הנדרים בשבת, כדאמרינן פרק מי שהחשיך (שבת דף קנז.)? וי"ל, דלצורך שבת נשאלין, כדאמרינן התם; והאי הוי צורך שבת, שיהיה מותר לשתות יין בשבת:
Tosafot on Eruvin 30b:11:1.english: "Rather, Summakhos agrees with the Rabbis" - And if you say: For this reason as well, a nazirite should not [be able to] establish an eiruv with wine, since asking [to dissolve] vows on Shabbat is a rabbinic prohibition [shevut], as we say in the chapter [entitled] "Mi SheHechshikh" (Shabbat 157a)? And one can say: For the needs of Shabbat, one may ask [about vows], as we say there; and this constitutes a need of Shabbat, so that it will be permitted [for him] to drink wine on Shabbat.

Tosafot on Eruvin 30b:14:1.hebrew: תרגומא אחולה ואזקן - וא"ת: ולוקמא נמי כרבנן דסומכוס, ו"הכל לפי מה שהוא אדם" — אחולה ואזקן; דלרבנן מערבין חולה וזקן כדי מזונן, דמקילי טפי מסומכוס, דאמרי: אפילו במידי דלא חזי ליה מערבין משום דחזי לאחריני, כל שכן דמערבין במידי דחזי ליה אע"ג דלא חזי לאחריני? וי"ל: דלרבנן אין מערבין לחולה ולזקן כדי מזונן, אלא בסעודה בינונית; דהא כיון דלא בעו מידי דחזי ליה, אם כן לחולה וזקן מערבין נמי אפי' במאכל דלא חזי להו אלא לבריא, ובמידי דלא חזי לדידהו ע"כ שיעורו בסעודה בינונית, וא"כ גם במידי דחזי להו בעינן שיעור סעודה בינונית, דאין סברא שיהא לרבנן ב' שיעורין לחולה ולזקן. א"נ: "הכל לפי מה שהוא אדם" משמע נמי לאפוקי ישראל בתרומה. והא דנקט "תרגומא אחולה ואזקן" — הוא הדין דהוה מצי למינקט "אישראל בתרומה", אלא נקט חולה וזקן משום דרשב"א איירי ביה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 30b:14:1.english: Interpret it as referring to an ill and elderly person - And if you say: But let [the Gemara] establish [the Mishnah] even according to the Rabbis [who dispute] Summakhos, and [interpret] "all is according to the person" as referring to an ill and elderly person; for according to the Rabbis, one may establish an eiruv for an ill or elderly person with [only] enough for their sustenance, as they are even more lenient than Summakhos—for they say that even with an item that is not fit for him one may establish an eiruv because it is fit for others, all the more so that one may establish an eiruv with an item that is fit for him even though it is not fit for others? And one can say: According to the Rabbis, one does not establish an eiruv for an ill or elderly person with [only] enough for their sustenance, but rather with an average meal. For since they do not require an item that is fit for him [personally], if so, for an ill or elderly person one may also establish an eiruv even with food that is fit not for them but [only] for a healthy person; and with an item that is not fit for them, perforce its measure is an average meal. And if so, even with an item that is fit for them, we require the measure of an average meal, as it is unreasonable that according to the Rabbis there would be two [different] measures for an ill and elderly person. Alternatively: "All is according to the person" implies also excluding an Israelite [establishing an eiruv] with teruma. And that which [the Gemara] formulated: "Interpret it as referring to an ill and elderly person" — the same applies that it could have formulated: "[Interpret it as referring] to an Israelite with teruma"; rather, it formulated [its answer in terms of] an ill and elderly person because Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar was dealing with him.

Tosafot on Eruvin 30b:18:1.hebrew: ומר סבר אהל זרוק שמיה אהל - דוקא כשמונח הוי אהל, אבל בשעת זריקה אפילו רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה מטמא, דבאותה שעה לא חשיב אהל כלל, מידי דהוה אעוף פורח ואטלית המנפנפת, דתנן באהלות (פ"ח מ"ה) דאין מביאין ואין חוצצין. והכי נמי קתני בברייתא דמייתי בנזיר בפרק כהן גדול (נזיר דף נה.): ר' יוסי ברבי יהודה אומר, תיבה שהיתה מלאה כלים, זרקה באהל המת — טמאה, ואם היתה מונחת — טהורה. וא"ת: למ"ד אהל זרוק לא שמיה אהל, מה היו מועילים דלתות שתחת התינוקות מפני קבר התהום, כדאמר בפרק הישן (סוכה ד' כא.)? הא אהל זרוק הוא! ואומר ר"ת, שיסבור שלא היו מביאין דלתות, אלא שוורים שכריסם רחבה, כדא"ר יהודה התם; והשוורים רחמנא קרינהו אהל, דכתיב: "ובעצמות וגידים תסוככני" (איוב י). ורשב"א מפרש: דלתות על גב שוורים לכ"ע הוי אהל, דתנן באהלות (פ"ו מ"א): "אדם וכלים נעשים אהל לטמא אבל לא לטהר", פירוש: מביאין טומאה ואין מפסיקין בין טומאה שתחתיהם לכלים שעליהם; ולא מיירי באדם וכלים שעושים עצמן אהלים, אלא כדמפרש התם: כגון נדבך של אבנים או דלתות על האדם או על הכלים, אפילו כלי גללים וכלי אבנים וכלי אדמה; ומשמע דסבר דאהל זרוק לא שמיה אהל, דאי שמיה אהל, כשנתן הנדבך על גבי הכלים אמאי לא יהיה חשוב אהל להפסיק? והא כלי עצמו נעשה אהל להפסיק כשאינו מקבל טומאה, כגון שידה תיבה ומגדל, למ"ד שמיה אהל! וקתני סיפא: "נתון על גבי אבנים שאינם כלים או על דבר שיש בו רוח חיים" — דומיא דשוורים בפרק הישן (סוכה ד' כא.) — "טומאה תחתיו כלים שעליו טהורין כו'", משמע דבענין זה הוי אהל לכ"ע:
Tosafot on Eruvin 30b:18:1.english: And the Master holds that a moving tent is called a tent - Specifically when it is at rest is it a tent, but at the time of throwing [or while in motion], even Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, deems [it] impure, for at that time it is not considered a tent at all, just as it is with a flying bird or a flapping cloak, as we learned in a mishna in Oholot (8:5) that they neither bring [impurity] nor interpose [to shield from it]. And so too it teaches in a baraita cited in Nazir in the chapter [entitled] Kohen Gadol (55a): "Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says: A chest that was full of vessels, [if] one threw it into a tent containing a corpse — it is impure; but if it was resting — it is pure." And if you say: According to the one who holds that a moving tent is not called a tent, what benefit was provided by the doors that were underneath the children against a grave of the deep [a hidden grave], as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] HaYashen (Sukkah 21a)? For is that not a moving tent! And Rabbeinu Tam says that he would maintain that they did not bring doors, but rather oxen whose bellies were wide, as Rabbi Yehuda said there; and the Merciful One called oxen a tent, as it is written: "And with bones and sinews You screened me" (Job 10:11). And the Rashba explains: Doors upon the back of oxen are considered a tent according to everyone. For we learned in a mishna in Oholot (6:1): "A person and vessels become a tent to transmit impurity, but not to purify" — the explanation being: they bring impurity and do not interpose between impurity that is beneath them and vessels that are upon them; and it is not dealing with a person and vessels that make themselves into tents, but rather as it explains there: for example, a row of stones or doors [placed] upon the person or upon the vessels, even [vessels of] dung, stone vessels, or earthen vessels; and it implies that [the Tanna] holds that a moving tent is not called a tent, for if it were called a tent, when one placed the row upon the vessels, why would it not be considered a tent to interpose? For the vessel itself becomes a tent to interpose when it does not contract impurity, such as a chest, box, or cupboard, according to the one who holds [a moving tent] is called a tent! And the latter clause teaches: "[If it is] placed upon stones that are not vessels, or upon a living creature" — similar to the oxen in the chapter [entitled] HaYashen (Sukkah 21a) — "[if there is] impurity beneath it, vessels that are upon it are pure, etc." This implies that in this manner, it is considered a tent according to everyone.

Tosafot on Eruvin 30b:8:1.hebrew: תרומה נמי אפשר דמתשיל - ולא מצי לאוקמה בתרומה ביד כהן, דתו לא מצי לאתשולי עליה, כדאמר בפרק הנודר מן הירק (נדרים דף נט.) — מדקתני "בחולין", משמע: דווקא בחולין, אבל בתרומה, אפי' ביד ישראל — לא:
Tosafot on Eruvin 30b:8:1.english: "In the case of teruma as well, one can ask" - And [the Gemara] could not establish [Summakhos's statement as referring to] teruma in the possession of a priest, where one can no longer ask [a Sage] to annul it, as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] HaNoder Min HaYarak (Nedarim 59a) — because since [the Mishnah] teaches "with non-sacred [food]," this implies: specifically with non-sacred [food], but with teruma — even in the possession of an Israelite — no.

Tosafot on Eruvin 30b:9:1.hebrew: ולפרוש עליה ממקום אחר - השתא ס"ד דכל דבר שהוא משום שבות, לא גזרו עליו בין השמשות. ואף על גב דרבה, דאית ליה הכנה, אמרינן בפירקא (דף לח:) דתחילת היום קונה עירוב, וכוותיה קיימא לן — מ"מ מותר לתקן הטבל, דלא גזרו עליו בין השמשות, עד שתהא לילה ניכרת וידוע. והא דתנן בבמה מדליקין (שבת דף לד.) דספק חשיכה אין מעשרין את הודאי, והיינו כרבנן דר' — אפ"ה קס"ד דהך מתני' דהכא אתיא כרבי, משום דאיכא משניות טובא דמוקי להו הש"ס לקמן כרבי. וא"ת: אם כן, אמאי קתני מתני': "אבל לא בטבל"? הא חזי לתקוני בין השמשות! ואין לומר דההיא אתיא דלא כרבי — מדפריך לקמן (עירובין דף לד:): "רישא רבי וסיפא רבנן", ולא פריך: "רישא וסיפא רבנן ומציעתא רבי"; ועוד, דפריך לקמן: "אבל לא בטבל — פשיטא!", משמע דליכא מאן דפליג. ומיהו איכא למימר: הא דפריך "פשיטא" — היינו משום דמרישא שמעינן לה, דקתני: "מערבין בדמאי", דמשמע: אבל לא בטבל. וי"ל, דאינו מועיל מה שראוי לתקנו, אלא במידי דחזי השתא לשום אדם, כגון תרומה דחזיא לכהנים; ותדע, דאמר לעיל דאין מערבין בהקדשות, אף על גב דאפשר לאיתשולי עלייהו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 30b:9:1.english: "And let him separate for it from somewhere else" - Now, it entered [the Gemara's] mind that regarding anything that is [prohibited] due to a rabbinic decree [shevut], [the Sages] did not decree against it during twilight. And even though according to Rabba, who maintains [the prohibition of] preparation [hakhana], we say in [this] chapter (38b) that [the arrival of] the beginning of the day acquires the eiruv, and we hold in accordance with him — nevertheless, it is permitted to fix the tevel, for they did not decree against it during twilight until the night is distinguishable and definite. And as for that which we learned in [the chapter] "Bameh Madlikin" (Shabbat 34a), that at doubtful darkness [i.e., twilight] one may not tithe definite [untithed produce, vadai], and that is according to the Rabbis [who dispute] with Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] — even so, it entered [the Gemara's] mind that this Mishnah here follows Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], because there are many mishnayot that the Gemara later establishes as following Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi]. And if you say: If so, why does the Mishnah teach: "but not with tevel"? Isn't it fit to be fixed during twilight?! And one cannot say that that [clause] follows [the Rabbis and] not Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] — for from [the fact] that the Gemara objects later (34b): "[Can it be that] the first clause is Rabbi and the latter clause is the Rabbis?", and it does not object: "[Can it be that] the first clause and the latter clause are the Rabbis, and the middle clause is Rabbi?!"; and furthermore, that [the Gemara] objects later (31b): "'But not with tevel' — [isn't that] obvious?!", which implies that there is no one who disputes [it]. However, one could say: That which it objects "[isn't that] obvious?!" is because from the first clause we learn it, as it teaches: "One may establish an eiruv with demai," which implies: but not with tevel. And one can answer that [the fact] that it is fit to be fixed is effective only with regard to something that is currently fit for some person, such as teruma, which is fit for priests; and know [that this is so], as [the Gemara] said above that one may not establish an eiruv with consecrated items, even though it is possible to seek [annulment] for them.

Tosafot on Eruvin 30b:9:2.hebrew: לא נחשדו חברים - אע"ג דמשום כבוד שבת שרי, כדאמר בהאשה רבה (יבמות דף צג.) — היינו שצריך לאכול אותן פירות בשבת; אבל הכא מיירי דאין צריך לאוכלן בשבת. ואע"ג דאין מערבין אלא לדבר מצוה, לא התירו לתרום שלא מן המוקף אלא לכבוד שבת, ולא לצורך מצוה אחרת:
Tosafot on Eruvin 30b:9:2.english: Ḥaverim are not suspected - Even though for the honor of Shabbat it is permitted [to separate terumah not in proximity], as [the Gemara] says in [the chapter entitled] HaIsha Rabbah (Yevamot 93a) — that is [only when] one needs to eat that produce on Shabbat; but here we are dealing with [a case where] one does not need to eat it on Shabbat. And even though one may establish an eruv only for the sake of a mitzvah, they permitted separating [terumah] not in proximity only for the honor of Shabbat, and not for the purpose of another mitzvah.
